title: Edge handoff sidecar scrapbook — weekly notes and blockers
content:
Weekly scrapbook: quick hits from the field + weirdness we're tracking. Mostly raw; use as running log for handoff follow-ups.

High level summary:
- Two active onprem installs (Zephyr Labs, Meridian Finance) with sidecar health flapping after node drain events.
- One VPC customer (Northbridge) reporting packet drops at MTU boundary with tcpdump evidence across AWS Transit Gateway.
- Installer PR 1187 landed (sidecar: graceful shutdown backoff) — needs canary on dedicated pool before broadly enabling.

Standup 2026-07-22 (12:00 PT) — attendees: Maya, Liam, Asha, Diego, SRE oncall
- Zephyr: sidecar cert chain mismatch on load balancer -> sidecar rejects mTLS from customer LB. Root cause suspected: LB is truncating SAN entries on cert rotation. Repro steps attached in ENG-6720.
  - Temporary fix: add fallback cert with stripped SANs (Asha) — due 2026-07-23 EOD.
  - Long term: healthcheck update to surface cert mismatch vs. TLS handshake failure (Liam).
- Meridian: node drain + kube-proxy restart leads to non-zero conntrack entries causing HAProxy 502s for ~30s. Observed that kubelet evict/drain ordering differs on older kernels.
  - Action: propose drain workaround script in installer to force conntrack flush before HAProxy reload (Diego) — prototype by 2026-07-24.
- Northbridge (VPC): intermittent MTU/DF issues across TGW when jumbo frames enabled at the edge. Packet capture shows ICMP fragmentation-needed messages not propagated. Cloud networking ticket opened with carrier; in-parallel plan is to force MTU 1436 on sidecar to avoid fragments (Maya).
  - Note: need to add MTU override flag to sidecar config schema (installer PR follow-up).

Telemetry and logs:
- Sidecar logs (Zephyr): repeated "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" immediately after cert rotation window (2026-07-21 03:14 UTC). Config shows rotated certs present on disk; handshake still fails.
- HAProxy metrics: 95th latency spike correlating with kube-proxy restart. Suggest adding a transient 503->502 mapping in console dashboard for easier triage.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add a preflight to detect LB cert SAN truncation patterns? (quick regex detection) — yes/no? (ops/solutions input needed)
- How aggressive can we be with conntrack flush in customer clusters? risk: flushing could break other long-lived flows. Need SRE buy-in.
- Policy for enabling graceful shutdown backoff by default: rollout plan requires metrics-based canary. Who owns rollout gating? (Product + SRE)

Decisions taken this week:
- Enable installer flag to set sidecar MTU per-deployment (opt-in). Short term to unblock Northbridge.
- Backoff PR will be enabled for the nightly canary pool next Tuesday (2026-07-27) and observed for 48h.

Action items (owners):
- Asha: deploy fallback cert workaround to Zephyr handoff and validate traffic (due 2026-07-23).
- Diego: draft conntrack-flush prototype script and open PoC branch (due 2026-07-24).
- Liam: add healthcheck telemetry fields for TLS mismatch, open GH issue to track (ENG-6719) (due 2026-07-25).
- Maya: create MTU override schema change PR + test matrix for AWS TGW (due 2026-07-26).
- SRE: decision thread on acceptable conntrack flush window (start thread in #pd-install-sre).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a sidecar "safety valve" that responds to healthcheck with explanatory headers ("X-Sidecar-Error: cert-mismatch") so product teams can signal fallbacks.
- could use a short-lived connection proxy to swallow conntrack churn while backend pods rotate (sketch in GH gist).
- When we get time: build a small install-checker that simulates node drain + lb reload to catch HAProxy 502s before handoff.

Customer-facing bits to prep:
- Quick email template for Zephyr explaining temporary cert approach + rollback instructions.
- Runbook snippet for Meridian ops: recommended drain sequence + how to run conntrack cleanup safely. Add to playbook at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/78901

Slack refs:
- #pd-install: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/PD_INSTALL/p16234
- thread: ENG-6720 notes @channel 2026-07-22 11:50PT

Misc notes / oddities observed:
- Two customer clusters are still running kernel 4.19 — we've historically optimised tooling for 5.x assumptions. Need to add kernel compatibility checklist to preflight.
- One install had iptables mode vs nft mismatch causing ephemeral service glitches — recorded in the install log (see linked artifact).

Next check-in: Friday 2026-07-24 standup 09:30 PT. Will try to have PoC branches linked in PR comments by then.

End of scrapbook entry.

-- Maya
